consumer: The frontend's threat indicator asking, per monster, 'has this monster noticed/targeted the avatar?' — an engine-computed awareness predicate (e.g. the monster's sees-avatar / has-avatar-as-target / hostile-aware state), not raw position.
scope: Per-monster awareness of the avatar (the engine's own seen/target/attitude computation for each monster in view), matched to the 'noticed the avatar' clause — not merely the monster's existence and raw position within the window.
decisive_source: src/arcopolis_export.cpp::write_entities (monsters window) — iterates g->all_monsters(), filters by in_export_window, and writes only index/type_id/pos_local/pos_abs/hp/hp_max/hallucination; it emits NO noticed/aware/target field, so the awareness predicate is absent from the surface.
divergence: Two monsters in-window of the same type at the same hp/pos: one has the avatar as its hostile target (engine awareness predicate true) and one is idle/unaware (false). The proposed surface reports them identically with no awareness flag, so 'has any monster noticed the avatar' is unanswerable and would be falsely re-derived from raw position.
